nuggets.text: Roy Kramer coached the Chippewas to the 1974 Division II title, then became SEC commissioner and oversaw the BCS's creation.
Former Chippewa Eric Fisher was a 225-pound two-star recruit and became the first MAC player drafted No. 1 overall.
Head coach Matt Drinkall played wide receiver at Iowa and later coached Army's offensive line.
Kelly/Shorts Stadium was the last MAC stadium to install permanent lights, which arrived before the 2006 season.
When Kelly/Shorts Stadium opened in 1972, it was among the first in Michigan to use artificial turf.
The Chippewas' stadium was first named for R. Perry Shorts, a banker and 1900 grad; coach Bill Kelly's name joined it in 1983.
Kelly/Shorts Stadium seats 35,127, the largest on-campus stadium in the Mid-American Conference.
The Chippewas went 7-6 in Matt Drinkall's first season and reached their first bowl since 2021.
Receiver Langston Lewis was third-team All-MAC last season with 43 catches for 596 yards.
The Chippewas and Colgate meet for the first time ever on Saturday in Mount Pleasant.
